brief.userPrompt: Tuesday, March 9, 2027, Eastern Time. At 06:40 the Tallis SOC saw a bulk export from the web store using CartBridge Commerce's API credentials; at 07:05 the CISO, Lena Hartmann, suspended the key. At 07:15 a post on a breach forum claims 1.9 million Tallis customer accounts with passwords and cards for sale and shows 200 sample rows. The exercise starts at 07:30 as Chief Communications Officer Marcus Delaney opens the Communications Cell in Conference Room 3B. Pressure points: the holding statement is due within 60 minutes and must say what is known, not known and being done; at 07:52 TechSignal Daily reporter Ines Okonkwo emails with a 10:30 deadline; at 08:10 the CISO verifies 38 of 40 sample rows as real accounts but cannot yet say how many were taken; the 08:20 holding statement says no payment information was involved, which is wrong because the export included payment tokens (full card numbers are not stored; Lakeview Payments holds them), so a correction naming what was wrong and what is right is needed by about 11:40; at 08:40 a viral social post claims passwords were stored in plain text (they are bcrypt hashes) and phishing emails from a look-alike domain offer a refund; at 09:00 the market opens and the stock falls 6 percent by 09:45; the Midwest Business Wire desk sends a bulletin at 09:20; Brightwater Markets' category manager Fiona Ledesma calls at 09:30; the customer care queue reaches 240 waiting calls; at 10:15 forensics shows 412,000 accounts, not 1.9 million, were exported between March 2 and March 8; the Disclosure Committee led by General Counsel Gerald Okafor meets at 11:00 and must decide whether the incident is material or not yet determined and whether to file Item 1.05, Item 8.01 or nothing yet with the 5:30 p.m. Eastern EDGAR cut-off in mind; Miami Valley 9 News asks for a live interview at noon; the Open Ledger Check fact-checkers ask about the plain-text claim; the customer email to 412,000 people can go out at 400,000 per hour; the team must decide on a press conference by 14:00 and meet The Valley Courier's 16:00 deadline. Decisions the toolkit forms cover: holding statement, release approval, reporter responses (on the record, background, decline), correction, press conference, platform takedown requests, escalation, materiality determination, disclosure and regulator notice. The SimCell plays reporters, the wire desk, the fact-checkers, the platform trust and safety team, Brightwater Markets, retail partners, customers and social media, state attorney general staff and investors. Spokesperson Dana Whitcombe speaks for the company; the numbers and wording must match across the statement, the customer email and the filing.
constraints: Every Tallis email address uses the exercise domain tallishome.example; reporters, outlets, the retailer and vendors use fictional .example domains; never a real outlet, platform handle, company or person.

Wire items follow the style of the fictional Midwest Business Wire (bulletin, update) and are marked as exercise products; statements follow the holding-statement structure (known, not known, being done, next update); a correction names what was wrong and what is right; times are Eastern Time.
Player roles are only those in the audience list; the CEO, Investor Relations, Customer Care, the retailer, reporters, fact-checkers, platforms, regulators and the public are played by the SimCell.

overview.theme: Speaking first without speaking wrong, correcting fast when you do, keeping the statement, customer email and filing on the same numbers, and deciding on materiality before all the facts are in.
overview.threat: At 06:40 ET on Tuesday, March 9, 2027, the Tallis security operations center in Dayton saw a bulk export of customer records from the web store. The export ran through the API credentials of the web store vendor, CartBridge Commerce, and CISO Lena Hartmann suspended the key at 07:05. At 07:15 a breach-forum post claimed that 1.9 million Tallis customer accounts were for sale with passwords and cards, and it showed 200 sample rows. In fact the exposed data covers web store account records, including bcrypt-hashed passwords and Lakeview Payments payment tokens but no full card numbers. Forensics will later show that 412,000 accounts were exported between March 2 and March 8. The incident also affects Tallis Rewards and customer care, the press and social channels, the retailer relationship and the company's SEC disclosure duties.

objectives.name: Communication
objectives.text: Demonstrate the ability to issue a holding statement within 60 minutes that separates what is known, not known and being done, then publish a correction by about 11:40 that names the wrong 'no payment information' line and states that Lakeview Payments tokens were exported.

objectives.name: Use of Doctrine
objectives.text: Demonstrate the ability to move every external statement through the TCCP 3 approval route (Writer drafts, CISO confirms facts, General Counsel clears, CCO approves, CEO sees, IR told) and record the approver and time on the statement log, even under the TechSignal Daily 10:30 deadline.

objectives.name: Decision Making
objectives.text: Demonstrate the ability to reach and record a materiality decision ('material' or 'not yet determined') at the 11:00 Disclosure Committee meeting, using the factors in TCIDC 4, and to choose Item 1.05, Item 8.01 or no filing before the 5:30 p.m. EDGAR cut-off.

objectives.name: Information Consistency
objectives.text: Demonstrate the ability to keep one time-stamped fact sheet, so that the newsroom page, company accounts, customer email and any 8-K all use the 412,000-account figure after the 10:15 forensic update, and to answer the plain-text-password claim and the 'refund' phishing under the TMPCDI 5 rumor protocol.

roles.name: Chief Communications Officer (COMMS)
roles.description: Owns communications strategy, approval of every external statement, the decision on a press conference by 14:00 and the choice of who speaks.
standingOrders: Approve: nothing goes out without your approval and a time on the statement log; speed never replaces the route.
Correct: when a statement turns out wrong, correct it fast and plainly, naming what was wrong and what is right, rather than letting it stand.
Align: no number goes public until it matches the fact sheet and whatever the Disclosure Committee will file.
Spokesperson: put the designated spokesperson forward for customer-facing questions; the CEO is never first.

roles.name: VP Corporate Communications (Writer)
roles.description: Owns the time-stamped fact sheet and drafts holding statements, corrections, message maps, Q&A and the customer email.
standingOrders: Fact Sheet: write only from the fact sheet; every line carries a time stamp and a source.
Unknown: if the fact sheet does not settle a claim, the text says 'we are investigating', never a reassurance.
Holding: in the CCO's absence you may approve holding statements only, and nothing more.

roles.name: Media Relations Manager (MEDIA)
roles.description: Manages every reporter call and email, the reporter log, deadlines, and the choice of on the record, background or decline with COMMS.
standingOrders: Log: record every reporter, question and deadline as it comes in, then return each call before its deadline, even if only to decline.
Terms: state on the record or on background before you answer, and give no number that is not on the fact sheet.
Escalate: send live-interview requests and fact-checker questions to COMMS; do not commit the spokesperson yourself.

roles.name: Social Media Manager (SOCIAL)
roles.description: Manages company accounts, social listening, the listening report and platform takedown requests for impersonation and phishing.
standingOrders: Record: log each viral claim word for word, with the time and the account, and do not reply until COMMS approves.
Takedown: report look-alike phishing to the platforms with the URL and a screenshot, and send it to Security for the IC3 report.
Same Words: post only approved text, and use the same numbers as the newsroom page and the customer email.

roles.name: General Counsel (Disclosure Committee Chair)
roles.description: Owns clearance of statements on cause, scope, number of people affected, legal duty and fault, and chairs the Disclosure Committee on materiality and the 8-K.
standingOrders: Clear: clear holding statements in 20 minutes, not hours, and ask for a delay only for a stated legal reason.
Decide: make the materiality decision without unreasonable delay; if the facts are not enough, record 'not yet determined' and set a fixed time to reconvene.
Privilege: direct the forensic work through counsel, and keep conclusions about fault or vendor blame out of chat and email.
One Story: the filing, press statement, customer email and board update must use the same facts.

roles.name: CISO
roles.description: Owns verified technical facts on the CartBridge export, the work with Cardinal Forensics, and the reports to the FBI and CISA.
standingOrders: Verify: confirm technical facts by replying on the draft; an unconfirmed count is 'not yet known', not a guess.
Containment: keep the CartBridge key suspended and the logs preserved, even if the vendor or the business asks to restore service.
Coordinate: report to the FBI Cincinnati Field Office and CISA, and require CartBridge to coordinate its statements; do not blame the vendor in public.
Silent: give facts to the cell, never to the press.

phases.title: The Sample Rows
phases.goal: Tests whether the Communications Cell can open, get the CISO's facts in, and issue a holding statement within the TCCP 4 60-minute target. The statement must separate known, not known and being done, and must not claim more than the facts support.
beats: (07:30) The Communications Cell opens in Conference Room 3B under the CCO. The CISO briefs that the SOC in Dayton saw a bulk export at 06:40 through CartBridge Commerce API credentials and suspended the key at 07:05. Under TCIDC 4, the CISO also tells the CartBridge Commerce vendor in writing to preserve its logs. A breach-forum post from 07:15 claims '1.9 million accounts with passwords and cards' and shows 200 sample rows. Because an outside party claims to hold Tallis data, the CISO must call the General Counsel under the TCIDC 2 trigger.

Noise item: the 07:30 social listening report shows a burst of 'Tallis' mentions about an unrelated product recall rumor and a routine status.tallishome.example maintenance notice. SOCIAL must sort these out and keep the cell focused on 'Tallis breach' and 'Tallis hack'.

(07:52) Ines Okonkwo of TechSignal Daily emails MEDIA with screenshots of the forum post and a 10:30 deadline. The reply must go through the TCCP 3 approval route, and the approver and time must be recorded on the statement log.

(08:10) The CISO confirms that 38 of the 40 checked sample rows are real web store accounts but cannot say how many were taken. The CISO also notes that TSCDMD 2 says Tallis does not store full card numbers, which invites a too-broad 'no payment information' line.

(08:20) The Writer's holding statement built from the TMPCDI 3 template goes to the newsroom page and the company accounts (two-person approval in the social tool). The SimCell CEO asks whether 'no payment information was involved' can go in, and the line is published. This plants the error the cell must later correct.

phases.title: The Wrong Line
phases.goal: Business as usual breaks: rumors, phishing and market pressure arrive together. The cell must discover that its own published statement is wrong and start a correction, without repeating the false claims it is fighting.
beats: (08:40) A viral post claims Tallis stored passwords in plain text. At the same time, look-alike-domain emails offering customers a 'refund' and asking them to 'confirm card' start circulating. SOCIAL must apply the TMPCDI 5 rumor protocol and report the impersonation to the platforms' trust and safety teams (2–6 hour response).

Red herring: Rita Szabo of Consumer Notebook publishes customer screenshots of a 'strange charge'. These turn out to be ordinary order-confirmation complaints, and chasing them pulls MEDIA and the CISO away from the export facts.

Clue: the CISO's analysts share the export field list from the CartBridge API logs. It shows a Lakeview Payments payment-token column next to the bcrypt hash column. Next to the newsroom page on the room screen, this shows everyone that the 08:20 'no payment information' line is wrong.

(09:00–09:20) The market opens and the stock begins to fall (down 6 percent by 09:45). The web store reset counter passes 6,000 resets in an hour, against a normal 2,300 a week (TSCDMD 8). At 09:20 Paul Gaskill's Midwest Business Wire runs a bulletin quoting the forum's 1.9 million figure and the company's 'no payment information' line.
Customer care reports 240 calls waiting and asks for a script. The cell must decide what agents may say about tokens and passwords before the correction is approved.

phases.title: Numbers in Motion
phases.goal: Tests whether the cell can keep one time-stamped fact sheet while the facts change under it. The TechSignal deadline must be met, outside parties (retailer, vendor, law enforcement, insurer) must be managed, and the customer email must be prepared without sending it before the facts are confirmed.
beats: (09:30) Brightwater Markets category manager Fiona Ledesma calls the CCO and demands guarantees that shared customers are safe before Brightwater issues its own statement. Brightwater's message must match the Tallis fact sheet.

CartBridge Commerce emails a draft statement that implies Tallis mishandled the API key. Under TCIDC 8, the cell must coordinate its wording and avoid blaming the vendor in public. The CISO confirms that reports have been made to the FBI Cincinnati Field Office and CISA. The CFO is reminded to notify the cyber insurer through Midland Risk Partners within 24 hours.

(10:15) Cardinal Forensics revises the count from 1.9 million to 412,000 accounts, exported between March 2 and March 8. The Writer must update the fact sheet with a time stamp and flag every live product that still carries the old figure.

(10:30) The TechSignal Daily deadline arrives. MEDIA must deliver an approved reply that uses the 412,000 figure, names the payment tokens correctly and states when the next update will come (TCCP 4).

The Writer drafts the customer email to 412,000 accounts. Under TSCDMD 8 it may link only to a page on tallishome.example and must contain no button asking for a password. It cannot go out until Legal and the CISO agree on the wording (TCCP 4).

phases.title: One Set of Numbers
phases.goal: The exercise's main decision: at 11:00 the Disclosure Committee must determine materiality and choose a filing path under TCIDC 4. Then the cell must make sure the correction, newsroom page, accounts, customer email and any 8-K draft all use the same numbers.
beats: (11:00) DECISION POINT: the Disclosure Committee, chaired by General Counsel Gerald Okafor, weighs the TCIDC 4 factors: 412,000 accounts, payment tokens, a 6 percent stock drop, the retailer relationship and the many facts still unknown. It must record a decision of 'material' (file Item 1.05 within four business days) or 'not yet determined' (Item 8.01 or no filing yet before the 5:30 p.m. EDGAR cut-off). Each path has a cost: filing too early locks in unfinished facts; waiting risks an unreasonable delay and investor statements that do not match the filing.

The correction is published to the newsroom page and company accounts before about 11:40. It names the 08:20 'no payment information' line, states that Lakeview Payments tokens were exported and full card numbers were not, and gives the 412,000 figure. It must not repeat the plain-text claim as a headline.

Open Ledger Check asks for a statement and evidence on the plain-text-password claim. Jason Teller of Miami Valley 9 News asks for a live noon interview with B-roll of the campus. The CCO must decide whether spokesperson Dana Whitcombe appears, and with which approved numbers.

Technical hurdle: the email service shows the send to 412,000 will take about an hour at the 400,000-per-hour limit. The SimCell also reports a look-alike 'refund' email whose wording copies the draft. The cell must check the send timing and wording against the correction and the 8-K draft line by line.

(11:30) Tedious reconciliation: the Writer compares the statement log, fact sheet, newsroom page, social posts, customer care script, customer email and any filing draft for one set of figures and recorded approvers. ENDEX comes with the 14:00 press conference decision and The Valley Courier's 16:00 deadline handed off as open actions.

Go around the room one team at a time (Communications, Legal/IR, Security, Customer Care, Operations), write every answer on the whiteboard in two columns, and don't debate anything until all teams have spoken.

questions.text: At 1:25 (I-08), the export schema showing a populated Lakeview Payments token column went up on the cell screen. Next to it, your live newsroom page still said 'No payment information was involved.' Cardinal Forensics had already told you at 0:40 (I-04) that the 'card' column held tokens. At what moment did you stop trusting your own 08:20 statement? Who said so out loud? What kept the correction from going out sooner? And what in the 08:20 statement claimed something you didn't yet know, against the holding-statement rules?

At 1:42 (I-09b), Customer Care reported 240 callers waiting. Agents were reading the wrong 'no payment information' line word for word, and two had told callers the forum post was 'fake'. Chat macro CC-INC-02 went live at 10:20 with no CCO approval recorded. With the TechSignal Daily 10:30 deadline coming, which external words went through the TCCP 3 route (Writer, CISO, General Counsel, CCO, CEO sees, IR told), which skipped it, and why? What would a faster route for care scripts look like, one that still has an approver and a time on the log?

At 2:45 (I-15), Cardinal gave you a preliminary count of 412,000 accounts across 83 sessions from March 2 to 8, with high confidence but still being checked. Fifteen minutes later the Disclosure Committee met at 11:00. Did you record 'material' or 'not yet determined', and which TCIDC 4 factors drove that? How did you choose between Item 1.05, Item 8.01 or no filing before the 5:30 p.m. EDGAR cut-off? When did you bring in the law-enforcement or cyber task force contact, and what single piece of information would have let you decide faster?

At 2:15 (I-13), CartBridge offered a replacement key (cartbridge-integration-prod-r2) in 20 minutes, while admitting it still didn't know how the original key was used from outside your allow-listed IPs. It also planned an 11:00 statement putting the blame on Tallis's credential handling. Did operations and the security team understand each other's stakes: 3,400 unsynced orders and the 13:00 carrier cut-off against an attack path no one had explained? Did you treat the vendor key as evidence or as a ticket to close? And how did you answer the vendor's statement so it didn't contradict yours?

At 3:45 (I-21), the IR Director found five documents with five numbers: the correction draft and customer email said 412,000, the chat macro and the 8-K shell said up to 1.9 million, the talking points said roughly 400,000, and the 08:20 post was still pinned. Several approver fields were blank. Where was your single time-stamped fact sheet after the 10:15 forensic update, and who owned it? Why didn't every channel pull from it? And how did you handle the plain-text-password claim and the 'refund' phishing email under the TMPCDI 5 rumor protocol?

assumptions: The exercise is conducted in a no-fault learning environment. Its purpose is to test the Communications Cell's plans and procedures, not to grade the people who play.

The scenario is plausible, and events occur as they are presented. Players should not argue with the scenario. They should respond to it as if it were real, using what they know at the time of each module.

Players respond in accordance with existing plans, policies and procedures: the TCCP, the TCIDC, the TMPCDI and the TSCDMD. Where a plan is silent or unclear, players say what they would do and note the gap for the hot wash.

Players have only the information in the module narrative and the injects delivered to them. They do not know what later injects will find out, such as the cause, the attacker or the final account count.

Tallis Home Products, its vendors, retail partners, media outlets and every named external party are fictional. Exercise products, such as the materiality worksheet, are exercise aids and not legal advice.
artificialities: Time is compressed. Each module covers about one hour of exercise time, and the facilitator jumps the clock forward at 08:30, 09:30 and 10:30 Eastern Time. Some outside actions and actions done in parallel happen faster than they would in real life.

The Simulation Cell (SimCell) plays everyone outside the room. This includes the CEO, the Investor Relations Director, the Head of Customer Care and the Disclosure Committee secretary. It also includes Cardinal Forensics, CartBridge Commerce (the web store system vendor), Lakeview Payments, Brightwater Markets, Midland Risk Partners, the FBI Cincinnati and CISA (law-enforcement and cyber task force) contacts, reporters, the wire desk and the public.

The systems are named as they are in the plans but are not touched. The web store, the CartBridge API key, the SIEM, the email service, the social publishing tool, the newsroom page and EDGAR are all simulated. Nothing is published, sent, filed or suspended for real.

Injects arrive on paper, on the cell screen or by the facilitator reading them aloud. Phone calls, texts and emails are acted out or handed over. Social media, wire and news items are exercise products.
